title: Fix Accessibility
prompt:
This page looks fine in the preview, but it fails automated accessibility checks. Your job is to fix the accessibility problems, not redesign the page.

Press Run / Restart, then Grade. Read the accessibility issues in the results. Fix them in the HTML and Grade again until everything passes.

  • Give the document a language: set lang="en" on <html>.
  • Give the image a text alternative: add an alt attribute that describes the picture (for example A friendly cat). The image file is cat-v1.png (provided with the assignment).
  • Associate the text field with its label: use matching id / for values (the label already says Name).
  • Give the button an accessible name: put visible text inside the <button> (for example Save).

Note: Automated checkers catch many common mistakes but not every accessibility issue. Fix what Grade reports for this exercise.

html.starter:
Club signup

Welcome! Tell us your name and save.

tests.name: Accessibility checks pass
tests.feedback: Fix the accessibility issues listed in the test details (language, image alt, input label, button name).

tests.name: Image has alt text
tests.feedback: Add an alt attribute on the (for example alt="A friendly cat").

tests.name: Label is associated with the input
tests.feedback: Give the input an id and set the label's for attribute to that same id.

tests.name: Button has visible text
tests.feedback: Put the word Save inside the <button>.
